name: AD — DCSync: Directory Replication by an Unexpected Principal
description:
Attacker objective
Replicate the directory (DCSync) to pull password hashes for any account — including krbtgt — without touching a Domain Controller's disk.

Attack logic
The Directory Replication Service exposes the DS-Replication-Get-Changes(-All) control-access rights. Only Domain Controllers and sanctioned directory-sync services should exercise them; any other principal doing so is running DCSync (e.g. via Mimikatz).

Why this detection works
Object-access auditing (4662) records the replication access-control GUIDs and the requesting principal. Excluding Domain Controller computer accounts and sanctioned sync/identity services leaves only anomalous replication.

False positives
A directory-sync or identity-management service not yet in the exclusion, or a new Domain Controller. Human/interactive accounts triggering replication are almost never legitimate.

Tuning
Allowlist verified replication service accounts (identity sync, IGA tooling) after confirmation; investigate every human account that replicates.

Required telemetry
Windows Security 4662 with Properties containing the replication GUIDs (1131f6aa / 1131f6ad) and AccessMask 0x100. Requires directory-object replication-property SACL auditing (already enabled here).
author: raadabujaish
note:
## Investigation guide
1. SubjectUserName is the replicating principal; a non-DC, non-service account performing GetChanges is DCSync.
2. If confirmed, treat the domain as compromised: reset all privileged accounts and rotate KRBTGT twice.
3. Correlate with the host the principal logged on from and any preceding privilege escalation.
false_positives: A directory-sync or identity-management service not yet in the exclusion, or a new Domain Controller. Human/interactive accounts triggering replication are almost never legitimate.
query: event.code:"4662" and winlog.event_data.AccessMask:"0x100" and (winlog.event_data.Properties:*1131f6aa* or winlog.event_data.Properties:*1131f6ad* or winlog.event_data.Properties:*9923a32a*) and not winlog.event_data.SubjectUserName:(*$ or MSOL_* or manageengine or "ANONYMOUS LOGON")
